subheading: CLINICAL FEATURES OF CHRONIC STABLE ANGINA (ANGINA PECTORIS)
text:
CLINICAL FEATURES OF CHRONIC STABLE ANGINA (ANGINA PECTORIS)
Symptoms
Typically, retrosternal chest pain or heaviness worsened by exertion that
radiates to the left upper arm, and radiating into the neck. Also tightness of the
chest as if it is being tied
Angina equivalents include:
- Dyspnoea
- Palpitation
- Giddiness
- Fatigue
- Silent ischaemia may occur in the diabetics and the elderly
Signs
There may be no specific abnormal finding. Nicotine stain of the nails and
cardiomegaly may be observed
